claims: Artemis 2 is NASA’s first crewed mission of the Artemis program.
Artemis 2 will send four astronauts on a 10-day flyby around the Moon.
Artemis 2 will use the SLS rocket.
Artemis 2 will use the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis 2 marks the first human return to deep space in over 50 years.
The mission goal of Artemis 2 is to test the Orion spacecraft's life-support, communication, and navigation systems with a crew in deep space.
The crew of Artemis 2 consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The flight path of Artemis 2 is a 10-day, figure-eight, free-return trajectory around the Moon and back to Earth.
The Artemis 2 crew will perform manual, close-proximity maneuvers with the SLS rocket’s spent upper stage to test navigation.
The Artemis 2 crew will test systems while still in high Earth orbit.
Artemis 2 follows the uncrewed 2022 Artemis I flight.
Artemis 2 is a collaborative effort with international partners, including Japan and the European Space Agency.
Artemis 2 is the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft.
